title: the close gate resolves every AC/AT reference against the WORKING TREE and no lifecycle verb commits, so a thread closes PASS on canon that exists on one node's disk -- and unlike 0174 the wrong tree makes it pass, not refuse
body:
**THE CLOSE GATE TAKES ITS POPULATION FROM THE WORKING TREE, AND NO LIFECYCLE VERB COMMITS -- SO A THREAD CLOSES GREEN ON CANON THAT EXISTS ONLY ON ONE MACHINE'S DISK.**

Measured 2026-09-05 in Lamplight on ST0347. `intent ac gate ST0347` returned PASS 36/36, every work package green, and the entire close was uncommitted. It stayed that way through several re-runs of the gate, each one answering PASS, because each one was reading the same untracked bytes that made it PASS. Committed afterwards at Lamplight `5c39c9a3c`, at which point the answer became true rather than merely repeatable.

**BOTH HALVES ARE AT SOURCE AND NEITHER IS A BUG IN ITS OWN TERMS.**

`facade.rs:4126` builds the gate's reference resolver as `contract::RepoFiles(self.project.root())`, and `contract.rs:273-279` is the whole of it:

    fn resolves(&self, path: &str) -> bool { self.0.join(path).exists() }
    fn carries_id(&self, path: &str, at_id: &str) -> bool {
      std::fs::read_to_string(self.0.join(path)).is_ok_and(|text| text.contains(at_id))
    }

`.exists()` and `read_to_string` on the worktree. There is no git call on the gate path -- `contract.rs` contains the string `git` zero times. The thread itself arrives via `st_show`, which reads the store, which is derived from on-disk canon.

The other half: **no lifecycle verb commits.** `st done`, `wp done`, `ac`, `at` write canon and stop. Grepping the crates for `"commit"` returns only `write_set.rs` and `migrate.rs`, where `commit()` is the WriteSet's own filesystem transaction -- a different sense of the word, in the codebase that would need the other one.

Each half is defensible alone. Composed, they mean **the gate's subject is a filesystem and its verdict is read as a claim about the project.**

**THIS IS 0174 AND 0125 REFLECTED, AND THE REFLECTION IS THE POINT.** Those two are pre-commit guards reading the wrong tree and REFUSING -- a peer's uncommitted file reddens your commit. Loud, immediate, and diagnosed independently by three nodes the day it happened. This one reads the wrong tree and PASSES on your own uncommitted work. **A false refusal announces itself; a false pass is indistinguishable by inspection from a true one**, and the thread it closes goes on reading Completed forever. The fix for those was stated as "a population, not a predicate" and that is exactly what is wrong here too -- but the direction of harm inverts, so it needs its own row rather than a line on theirs.

**THE SHARED-CHECKOUT FACE IS WORSE THAN THE SINGLE-NODE ONE.** Five nodes work one Lamplight tree. Node A runs `intent ac gate ST0347` against its own uncommitted close and gets PASS. Node B runs the identical command, same repo, same second, and gets a different verdict -- and **nothing in either output names the tree it examined**, so there is no reading of the two results that reveals a population difference rather than a disagreement about the thread. The AT half compounds it: `carries_id` reads a cited test file's TEXT off the worktree, so an uncommitted test, or uncommitted edits to a committed one, satisfies a citation for whoever's disk holds it.

**THE REMEDY IS NOT SIMPLY 'READ HEAD'.** The gate is a read -- `pub fn gate` is documented "it changes nothing and refuses nothing" -- and its main use is answering *am I ready* while the work is still in your editor. A gate that only ever saw HEAD would answer no useful question during work. Two things separate:

- **The interactive read must SAY which tree it examined** -- one line, the way `canon_commit_check.sh` already narrows explicitly and reports its narrowing. A verdict that does not name its population cannot be compared across nodes, which is the whole defect above.
- **The status transition is where HEAD belongs.** `facade.rs:4582` gates `st done` on the same worktree read (`check_gate(("Thread", "status", op), ...)`), so a thread can transition to Completed on evidence no other node can see and no clone can reproduce. Closing is the moment the claim stops being about your afternoon.

**FILED SO THE COST IS RECORDED RATHER THAN RE-DIAGNOSED.** It cost nothing this time -- the close was correct and committing it made the green true. That is the bad case, not the good one: the failure mode never announced itself, and the only reason it was found is that a peer asked why the canon was dirty.
